title: Operational economics & reliability partner sync - Heliotrope Health
summary: Monthly partner health check focusing on usage trends, cost drivers, recent incidents and roadmap alignment. Customer is seeing steady adoption in clinical summarization flows but rising token spend on experimental QA workflows. Discussed batching, prefix caching, and Dedicated vs hosted routing for predictable SLAs. Agreed to run a focused benchmark on 5 clinical prompts and share optimized config and cost model.
topics: Roadmap sync and upcoming changes (runtime optimizations)
Next steps: benchmark, pricing, dashboard links
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Sofia P., Marcus L., Anika G. (Redwood) — Lena O., Rahul M., Maria G., Tom B., Priya D. (Heliotrope)

[00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — usage, costs, reliability incidents last three weeks, and then ops / roadmap. is that good?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: yep that works. thanks Sofia.
[00:12] Marcus Liu: will do a quick slide on what we saw in the infra side, but i want to call out the KV cache opportunity up front.
[00:18] Rahul Menon: and i'll jump in on the platform constraints — we're seeing some tail latency on long summaries.
[00:22] Sofia Patel: perfect. Anika, do you want to highlight the billing patterns?
[00:26] Anika Gupta: sure — so month-over-month token usage is +34% driven by the new QA assistant tests and the daily clinical summarizer. most of the extra cost is from the 32k-context experiments. there are also several retries logged which amplify billable tokens.
[00:40] Priya Das: the finance team flagged the spike last week. we need to understand predictable spend if we double usage.
[00:45] Sofia Patel: absolutely. on the cost side, common levers are batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles. Marcus will walk through some quick numbers.
[00:53] [05:00] Marcus Liu: ok — so we ran sampling on their average payloads. two things: first, continuous batching gives ~18% cost savings without affecting 95th pct latency for short flows. second, prefix/k-v cash — sorry, kv cache — for the clinical summarizer where the initial prompt is stable, we see up to 40% token savings for sessions that re-use prefixes.
[05:24] Rahul Menon: can you remind me how KV cache interacts with stateful sessions in Dedicated mode? we currently use the hosted api.
[05:28] Marcus Liu: yes — in Redwood Dedicated you can pin a cache to a model instance and get deterministic reuse. hosted also supports cache but eviction and cross-tenant policies vary; dedicated gives more control and better hit rates for your pattern.
[05:38] Tom Becker: we've had two incidents this month where a canary deploy caused increased latency. both were auto-rollback but users saw timeouts.
[05:44] Marcus Liu: do you have traces? A few things to check: kernel selection for long sequences, and batching windows. sometimes a rollout picks a quantized variant that behaves worse on corner sequences.
[05:54] Lena Ortiz: the incidents were during peak ingestion — about 3pm PST — with many concurrent summarization jobs. logs show a lot of 504s from our side then.
[06:00] Marcus Liu: sounds like capacity constraint + different model variant — could also be network bursts. we can correlate Redwood console traces to your traces if you share the request ids.
[06:08] Sofia Patel: action item: Lena to share two example request ids and timestamps. Marcus to correlate and report back.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: noted.
[06:14] [10:00] Anika Gupta: on reliability metrics, we've been tracking per-route p95 latency and error budget burn. your p99 for the summarizer spiked to 1.8s last Friday, normally around 0.6. that's what triggered the alert.
[10:24] Maria Gomez: is that at the Redwood layer or our upstream processing?
[10:28] Anika Gupta: a mix — the console shows a spike in inference latency, but there's also a queue backlog on your side at times.
[10:34] Rahul Menon: we can instrument better, but the question from infra is whether Dedicated would make this more predictable.
[10:38] Marcus Liu: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor effects and gives predictable throughput. if SLAs matter for clinical UIs, it's a common move. we can size a Dedicated pool to keep p95 under target at your projected peak.
[10:46] Priya Das: pricing — how different is Dedicated cost compared to hosted? our CFO wants a delta.
[10:50] Sofia Patel: we'll send a side-by-side: hosted marginal unit costs with current patterns vs Dedicated committed spend with burst options. approximate numbers today suggest Dedicated becomes cost-efficient if sustained peak is above ~20k tokens/sec equivalent for a month, but we'll model with your exact usage.
[11:08] [15:00] Marcus Liu: another optimization is using a quantization profile — 4-bit QAT for certain models reduces VRAM and can increase packing, lowering per-token cost. caveat: small quality delta in some prompts, so we recommend A/B evals.
[15:20] Lena Ortiz: can we run that A/B on clinical summaries? quality tolerance is low.
[15:24] Marcus Liu: yes — we'll run a pilot on 1,000 clinical prompts against current baseline and quantized variant.
[15:30] Sofia Patel: note: we'll need consent and de-identification for clinical content in the eval; please confirm scope.
[15:36] Lena Ortiz: we'll scrub PHI and provide consent — Rahul will coordinate.
[15:40] Rahul Menon: yep.
[15:42] [20:00] Tom Becker: curious about autoscaling — we've seen spikes where the platform didn't scale fast enough and front-ends timed out. is there a recommended autoscale policy?
[20:10] Marcus Liu: recommended starting point is a hybrid policy: baseline reserved capacity to cover 70-80% typical load, plus fast scale (short cooldown, aggressive step-up) for spikes. Dedicated supports instant burst lanes if pre-configured. For hosted, we suggest routing rules that fall back to a cheaper model variant rather than try to instantly scale infinitely.
[20:30] Maria Gomez: fallback to cheaper variant — what's the UX change? do clients get different answers?
[20:34] Marcus Liu: yes potential slight quality change; Redwood's rollouts can annotate responses with model metadata so you can detect when a fallback occurred.
[20:42] Priya Das: finance wants worst-case monthly cost for spikes — do you have estimates?
[20:46] Sofia Patel: we'll produce a cost simulation: baseline + 3 spike profiles (short sharp, sustained medium, sustained high). That'll be in the deck we share.
[20:56] [25:00] Anika Gupta: roadmap note — we're rolling out a runtime kernel optimization in late June that improves long-seq throughput ~12% on tested models. we'll flag which models and when. This should help the p99 tails.
[25:20] Lena Ortiz: great — will you send the list of affected models?
[25:24] Anika Gupta: yes, Marcus will add it to the benchmark pack.
[25:28] Marcus Liu: on benchmarks — proposal: we run a 48-hour benchmark with (a) your production traffic replay for the summarizer (sanitized), (b) 1k clinical prompts for quality A/B, (c) spike injection to test autoscale and fallback.
[25:48] Rahul Menon: timeline? we need results before the exec review on June 8.
[25:52] Marcus Liu: we can start the replay as soon as you provide sanitized logs; run is 48 hours and we'll aim to deliver a results summary within 5 business days after completion.
[25:58] Lena Ortiz: ok we'll aim to deliver logs by May 26.
[26:02] Sofia Patel: action: Rahul deliver sanitized logs by 2026-05-26. Marcus to run benchmark and deliver report by 2026-06-02.
[26:08] Rahul Menon: noted.
[26:10] [30:00] Maria Gomez: on governance — we need audit logs and SSO integration for new team members. are there any gaps?
[30:16] Sofia Patel: Redwood supports SAML SSO and has audit logs; we can enable token-level audit retention longer for enterprise. We also offer granular RBAC for routes and models.
[30:24] Tom Becker: any latency cost to long-term audit retention?
[30:28] Anika Gupta: only storage costs; logs are offloaded. no inference latency impact.
[30:32] Priya Das: also want to confirm encryption at rest with customer-managed keys — we have a requirement for KMS.
[30:38] Marcus Liu: yes, KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports bring-your-own-key in selected regions — we'll doc the exact options.
[30:46] [35:00] Sofia Patel: competitor note — you mentioned evaluating another vendor last quarter, correct?
[35:04] Lena Ortiz: yeah we had a brief PoC with CloudX. They were competitive on price but struggled with long-seq reliability.
[35:12] Maria Gomez: also did a small bench with InferenceCo; their telemetry was less mature.
[35:18] Marcus Liu: good input. we'll include comparative notes in the follow-up deck.
[35:22] [40:00] Sofia Patel: recap and next steps: 1) Rahul deliver sanitized logs by 2026-05-26; 2) Marcus run 48h benchmark + A/B and post results by 2026-06-02; 3) Sofia to share cost simulation and Dedicated vs hosted delta by 2026-05-25; 4) Lena to send two request ids for recent incidents for trace correlation by 2026-05-22; 5) Marcus to include list of models affected by June runtime kernel optimization; 6) Marcus to provision a short-lived Dedicated sizing estimate for exec review.
[40:30] Priya Das: finance will review the cost sim once received.
[40:34] Lena Ortiz: thx everyone. quick question — will the benchmark use masked clinical data or synthetic?
[40:38] Marcus Liu: by default masked/sanitized repo; if you prefer synthetic we can generate a close approximation. we'll follow whatever meets your compliance.
[40:44] Sofia Patel: last thing — we'll share links to the Redwood console dashboards and the security pack after this call.
[40:50] Anika Gupta: and i'll open a support ticket to track the incident correlating work.
[40:54] [45:00] Tom Becker: thanks all, that was helpful.
[45:04] Lena Ortiz: thanks team.
[45:08] Sofia Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the deck and action items. adjourn.
